name: Pramipexole Dihydrochloride
meta: 0.125 mg, 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1.5 mg; 0.75 mg & 3 mg (extended release)
sections: White to off-white powder (dihydrochloride monohydrate), freely soluble in water.

Approved for Parkinson's disease in 1997 and restless legs syndrome in 2006; extended-release once-daily tablets introduced in 2009–2010. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1997 (Pharmacia & Upjohn; developed by Boehringer Ingelheim).
0.125 mg, 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1.5 mg; 0.75 mg & 3 mg (extended release)

Full agonist at dopamine D2-family receptors with preferential D3 affinity; directly stimulates striatal dopamine receptors in Parkinson's disease and relieves restless legs syndrome. Receptor / target profile: Non-ergoline full agonist at D2-family receptors with highest affinity for D3 (Ki 0.5 nM).
Summary: Bioavailability >90%; Tmax ~2 h (ER ~6 h). ~15% protein bound. Minimal metabolism; excreted unchanged in urine. Half-life 8–12 h. Adjust dose in renal impairment.
Idiopathic Parkinson's disease – monotherapy or with levodopa
Moderate-to-severe primary restless legs syndrome (immediate release)
Parkinson's (IR, as salt): 0.125 mg three times daily for week 1, 0.25 mg TDS week 2, 0.5 mg TDS week 3; then increase by 0.75 mg/day weekly; max 4.5 mg/day
Parkinson's (ER): 0.375 mg once daily, increase every 5–7 days; max 4.5 mg once daily
Restless legs: 0.125 mg once daily 2–3 h before bedtime; increase every 4–7 days; max 0.75 mg
Renal impairment: reduce frequency per CrCl
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
PD IR: CrCl 20–50 – twice daily; <20 – once daily. ER: CrCl 30–50 – alternate days initially; <30 – not recommended.
Use only if clearly needed; may inhibit lactation.
Sudden sleep onset and somnolence – avoid driving if affected
With food to reduce nausea; avoid alcohol.
Sleep attacks; impulse-control behaviour; BP; skin (melanoma screening in PD).
Nausea, vomiting, hyperkinesia, hallucinations, agitation, hypotension. Supportive care; antipsychotic (dopamine antagonist) may be considered.
CALM-PD (Parkinson Study Group, JAMA 2000) – initial pramipexole caused fewer motor complications than levodopa.
Trials in restless legs syndrome (Winkelman et al., 2006).
Do not drive if you experience sudden sleepiness
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
